simple.meaning: פְּצָלָה (pᵉtsâlâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a peeling.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Genesis, beginning at Genesis 30:37. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פְּצָלָה (H6479) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: פְּצָלָה (pᵉtsâlâh) / H6479 is traced through Genesis 30:37 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Jacob took to himself rods of fresh poplar, almond, and plane tree, peeled white streaks in them, and made the white appear which was in the rods.
